nodes.label: iPhone
nodes.rationale: Pro iPhones with LiDAR get the floor map; other phones fall back to the 0.5x ultra-wide camera and the gyro for turns.

nodes.label: Models
nodes.rationale: Everything runs on one RTX 4090 except what Apple does on the phone; all models are open weights.

nodes.label: Pip
nodes.rationale: Prototype built at Hacktoberfest Hack Day San Diego, not a mobility aid: use it with a cane or guide dog, not instead of them. Guides mostly with taps and talks only when something changes (a turn, a door, an obstacle, arriving).

nodes.label: Server deploy over Tailscale (tools/deploy.sh)
nodes.rationale: Stops every running copy of Pip on the PC (the scheduled task, its restart loop, every API and both llama-servers; nothing else), restarts and warms the models; the previous app.py is kept as app.py.bak-<time>.

nodes.label: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads (App Transport Security off)
nodes.rationale: Lets the app talk plain HTTP to the model server on the local network.

nodes.label: Arrival check (room proof in 3 frames + vision model agrees)
nodes.norm_label: arrival check (room proof in 3 frames + vision model agrees)
nodes.rationale: A room counts only when the detector sees proof (a toilet for a restroom) in 3 frames in a row and the vision model agrees you're inside, not just looking in through a doorway.

nodes.label: Backtrack and retry (asks after 3 backtracks or 6 look-arounds)
nodes.norm_label: backtrack and retry (asks after 3 backtracks or 6 look-arounds)

nodes.label: Door coaching (vision reads door type, LiDAR detects it opening)
nodes.norm_label: door coaching (vision reads door type, lidar detects it opening)
nodes.rationale: Vision reads the door once (hinge knuckles on your side mean pull; push plate or door stop means push) and guides the hand to the handle. LiDAR detects the moment it opens because it suddenly sees past it; glass fools LiDAR, so glass and automatic doors keep the camera check. A door that won't open after 45 s, or that you say is locked, is skipped.

nodes.label: Getting out first (leave the building before the GPS route)
nodes.norm_label: getting out first (leave the building before the gps route)
nodes.rationale: GPS is weak indoors, so Pip maps the room, picks a real door or opening, drops a mark and checks progress only at decision points because the numbers jump while walking. An exit sign overrides measurements. Outside only when GPS has been good for a few seconds and the camera agrees, because Wi-Fi location can look good indoors.

nodes.label: All sound through native iOS audio
nodes.norm_label: all sound through native ios audio
nodes.rationale: If WebKit plays audio it switches the audio session to playback-only and the mic stops listening.

nodes.label: Short-term planner (A* path to taps and clock-face phrases)
nodes.norm_label: short-term planner (a* path to taps and clock-face phrases)

nodes.label: Unknown places exploration (floor map doors, openings, signs, look around)
nodes.norm_label: unknown places exploration (floor map doors, openings, signs, look around)
nodes.rationale: The brain must pick one of the real candidates by id so it cannot invent a door; a matching sign read on the phone wins over a guess. Without LiDAR, 8 photos during a slow turn are described and the brain picks the most promising way.

nodes.label: Clean code contract
nodes.rationale: Checked on this Mac only; there is no GitHub CI.

nodes.label: Cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: Delete what Claude made once it is replaced and unused, in the same task; never delete user/other-session work, trips/ recordings or git history without asking; report deletions.

nodes.label: Comments explain why, not what
nodes.rationale: A new tuning number gets its unit and where the value came from.

nodes.label: Design-first rule
nodes.rationale: Any change to what the screen shows (label, button, status line, color) goes into pen.dev before the code.

nodes.label: Don't hide errors
nodes.rationale: A catch handles or logs the error (log() in the app so it lands in the trip log, logging in the server); empty catches only for cleanup allowed to fail.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge-graph contract
nodes.rationale: Query the graph before reading code; update it after changes; graph.json is rewritten whole so big diffs are expected; it skips design/tokens.json because "tokens" looks like a secret.

nodes.label: Names say what things do
nodes.rationale: Short names only for the existing app-wide objects S (app state) and N (phone sensor data).

nodes.label: No dead code rule
nodes.rationale: No unused functions, icons or CSS, no commented-out code, no console.log/print; git keeps old versions.

nodes.label: No new dependencies without asking
nodes.rationale: Web app is plain JavaScript with no build step or npm; tools/ uses only the Python standard library; the iPhone app uses only Apple frameworks; server packages are in server/requirements.txt.

nodes.label: pen.dev design contract
nodes.rationale: design/untitled.pen is the single source of truth for how Pip looks.

nodes.label: Sound and speech rules (frontend/app.js)
nodes.rationale: Taps, ticks and speech are not in the design; they follow research-based rules in frontend/app.js.

nodes.label: Testing contract: Mac vs phone
nodes.rationale: Screens, builds, speech and server replies are tested on the Mac; Pip's main job needs a person moving through a real place, so no simulated walks: the user tests on the phone and Claude diagnoses from the real trip recording.

nodes.label: Directional tap guidance (ear-side taps that speed up as you face the target)
nodes.norm_label: directional tap guidance (ear-side taps that speed up as you face the target)
nodes.rationale: A tap in the left ear means turn left; taps speed up as you get closer to facing the right way, and on course it goes quiet or ticks softly in both ears, so speech is saved for changes.
